topics.label: Introduction and Course Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the course structure, learning outcomes, and broad clinical context of cancer biology.

topics.label: Cancer as a Failure of Differentiation and Tissue Architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain that cancer arises from a breakdown of normal differentiation and three-dimensional tissue organization driven by genetic alterations, and discuss the methods used to study this biology.

topics.label: Invasion, Metastasis, and Benign versus Malignant Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how tissue invasion and metastasis distinguish malignant tumors from benign lesions, using histological models of stepwise progression.

topics.label: Neoplasm Nomenclature and Classification
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the standard linguistic conventions and exceptions used to name benign and malignant tumors according to their tissue of origin.

topics.label: Pathophysiological Mechanisms of Cancer Illness and Death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how local anatomical disruption, metabolic complications, and metastatic organ colonization cause clinical disease and patient mortality.

topics.label: Cancer Incidence and Comparative Oncology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyse the epidemiological prevalence of major tumor types in humans and compare tumor incidence across various animal taxa.

topics.label: Cancer Detection and Population Screening Methods
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the diagnostic principles, histological indicators, and practical outcomes of screening programs across different cancer types.

topics.label: Conclusion and Next Steps
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a review of learning objectives and reminders for upcoming practical sessions.
